parties.appellant_or_petitioner: in Cri, A. No. 37673-J/2022 and M.R. No, 154/2022) Wasim Abbas

holding: Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, J. The petitioner-convict, Wasim Abbas, was tried and convicted by the Trial Court under section 302(b) PPC and sentenced to death as ta’zir, alongwith a direction to pay Rs.500,000/- as compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased under section 544-A Cr.P.C., or in default thereof to undergo six months S.I. He was further convicted under section 449 PPC and sentenced to undergo ten years R.I. with a fine of Rs.50,000/- or in default thereof to undergo six months S.I., with all sentences ordered to run concurrently. He challenged his convictions and sentences before the Lahore High Court, but his appeal was dismissed and his death sentence was confirmed vide “impugned judgment dated 20.06.2025, which has now been assailed before us through the instant jail petition. 2 The brief facts, as emerging from the record, are that on 11.10.2020 at about 3:00 p.m., the petitioner, armed with a .30 bore pistol, alongwith two unidentified accomplices on a motorcycle, trespassed into the house of the complainant, Mst. Irshad Begum (PW-8). The petitioner entered the room where the deceased, Shehnaz Bibi (his former wife), and Mst. Naeem Bibi (PW-9) were lying on charpoys, and after taunting the deceased about her demand for divorce, fired multiple shots at her. The petitioner inflicted six firearm wounds on her abdomen, hand, thighs, and back, while his unidentified accomplice fired an additional shot below her right knee, causing her to succumb to her injuries at the spot before fleeing. The motive behind this brutal occurrence stems from deep-seated resentment on the part of the petitioner as the deceased had instituted a suit for dissolution of marriage against him which culminated in an ex parte decree passed in her favor on 09.10.2020, merely two days prior to the murder. 3. The ocular account has been furnished by Mst. Irshad Begum (PW- 8) and Mst. Naheem bibi (PW-9) who happened to be inmates of deceased’s parental house and their evidence is found reliable, trustworthy and confidence inspiring. In the cases of murder occurring within domestic premises, the immediate family members of the deceased are the most natural witnesses and their evidence, if found reliable and corroborated by surrounding circumstances, ought to be accepted. In the instant case, the occurrence being taken place during broad daylight, drastically reduce or eliminate the possibility of mistaken identity as the witnesses had an unobstructed and clear view of the petitioner committing the offence in question. Even otherwise, the petitioner, being the former husband of the deceased, was known to the witnesses by name, face and association. Admittedly, the prosecution witnesses are closely related to the deceased, however, their evidence cannot be discarded merely on the basis of their relationship because it would mean that crimes committed within the domestic premises could never be prosecuted, which would be contrary to the ends of justice. 4. The petitioner was arrested and subsequently led the police to the place of concealment of the crime weapon which was recovered on his pointation. The empties recovered from the place of occurrence were subjected to ballistic examination and matched with the recovered weapon. It lends a strong support to the ocular account. Besides the medical evidence, which constitutes strong corroboration of the prosecution’s case, the motive in the present case is established beyond any shadow of doubt. The deceased obtained a decree of dissolution of marriage from the Family Court immediately before the occurrence. The petitioner’s inability to accept this dissolution, his resentment at the court decree and his desire for retribution are patent from the temporal proximity of the events. 5. The deceased exercised her lawful and legally recognized right under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 and the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 to seek dissolution of the marriage that had become intolerable. The State is under a constitutional obligation under Article 9, 14 and 25 of the Constitution to protect the life, dignity and equal treatment of all citizens, including women. This Court in the case of Shazia Perveen v State (PLD 2019 SC 474) emphasized as under: “4 woman who seeks legal dissolution of marriage through proper judicial process is exercising a fundamental right. Any violence perpetrated against her for exercising such right strikes at the very heart of the constitutional order and must be met with the full rigour of the law.” 6. Regarding the quantum of sentence, we find no extenuating or mitigating circumstances that could warrant any leniency or the commutation of the death penalty. The offense was perpetrated by the petitioner in an exceptionally brutal, calculated, premeditated, and cold- blooded manner inside the sanctity of the deceased’s home. The fact that the petitioner murdered his former wife merely forty-eight hours after she successfully secured a judicial decree for the dissolution of their marriage emphasizes a ruthless defiance of the law. In cases involving such deliberate acts of violence against women seeking their legal and marital rights, the capital penalty is fully justified to uphold the rule of law and satisfy the ends of justice. Ms We have scrutinized the record with anxious care, as is required in a matter involving the sentence of death/life imprisonment. We find no perversity in the findings and misreading of evidence. The findings of the courts below are well reasoned, based on proper appreciation of the entire evidence and are in consonance with the record. This Court, being mindful of the constitutional imperative to protect the life and dignity of women and to ensure that those who exercise their lawful rights are not subjected to violence with impunity, finds no basis to interfere with the concurrent conviction. 8. For all the reasons recorded above, this petition being devoid of merit is dismissed and leave is refused. ISLAMABAD 10.06.2026 (M. Qasim Najam, LC) Approved for Reportin:
